경찰.x: I got lost, so I asked a police officer.
경찰.e: 경찰서 = police station; 경찰관 = police officer.

작다.x: My room is a bit small.
작다.t: 작다 = small in size; 적다 = few or little in amount. Don't mix them up!

경기.x: I watched a soccer game until late last night.
경기.t: Homonym: 경기 also means 'the economy' (경기가 나빠요), and 경기도 is the province around Seoul.

경기.ex: 요즘 경기가 안 좋아서 장사가 힘들어요.
경기.x: Business is tough these days because the economy is bad.
경기.e: Literally 'view of the atmosphere' — the general mood of the economy.
경기.t: Homonym: 경기 (競技) also means a sports game; 경기가 좋다 is about the economy.

숙소.x: Our place was close to the beach, which was really nice.
숙소.t: Pronounced [숙쏘] — ㅅ after ㄱ becomes tense.

동료.ex: 회사 동료들과 같이 점심을 먹으러 갔어요.
동료.x: I went to have lunch with my coworkers.
동료.t: Pronounced [동뇨] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

장미.x: I got roses from my boyfriend on my birthday.
장미.e: From an old two-syllable Chinese word for the rose; the syllables aren't reused elsewhere.
장미.t: Count flowers with 송이: 장미 한 송이 'one rose'.

상추.x: Pork belly tastes best wrapped in lettuce.
상추.e: Usually traced to Sino-Korean 생채 'raw vegetable'; today it is felt as a native word.
상추.t: At Korean BBQ you wrap meat, garlic and 쌈장 (dipping paste) in a lettuce leaf; this kind of wrap is called 쌈, so a lettuce wrap is 상추쌈.

농부.x: My grandfather worked as a farmer in the countryside.

득점.ex: 그 선수가 이번 경기에서 가장 많은 득점을 했어요.
득점.x: That player scored the most points in this game.
득점.t: Pronounced [득쩜] — ㅈ after ㄱ becomes tense.

장바구니.m: shopping basket, reusable shopping bag; online shopping cart
장바구니.x: I carry a reusable shopping bag instead of plastic bags.
장바구니.e: 장 'market' (as in 장을 보다 'go grocery shopping') + native 바구니 'basket.'
장바구니.t: On shopping websites, 장바구니 is the 'cart' button.

방지하다.ex: 사고를 방지하기 위해 안전 교육을 합니다.
방지하다.x: We hold safety training to prevent accidents.

체크아웃.ex: 내일 아침 열한 시까지 체크아웃해야 해요.
체크아웃.x: We have to check out by 11 tomorrow morning.
체크아웃.t: Late check-out is 레이트 체크아웃. Many hotels will keep your bags after check-out: 짐 좀 맡겨도 될까요?

꼬르륵.x: I'm so hungry my stomach is growling.
꼬르륵.e: Sound word (의성어) for a rumbling stomach, or liquid gurgling through a narrow opening.
꼬르륵.t: Almost always 배에서 꼬르륵 소리가 나다; 배가 꼬르륵거리다 also works.

어리숙하다.ex: 그는 어리숙해 보여도 사실 아주 똑똑해요.
어리숙하다.x: He may look naive, but he's actually very smart.
어리숙하다.t: 어수룩하다 is an equally standard variant with the same meaning.

이타적.ex: 그는 늘 남을 먼저 생각하는 이타적인 사람이에요.
이타적.x: He's an altruistic person who always thinks of others first.
이타적.e: Literally 'benefiting others'; the opposite, 이기적, is 'benefiting oneself.'

확보하다.ex: 공연을 보려고 일찍 가서 좋은 자리를 확보했어요.
확보하다.x: I went early to the show and secured good seats.
확보하다.t: Pronounced [확뽀하다]; common objects: 자리, 예산, 인력, 증거.

생소하다.ex: 처음에는 한국 음식이 생소했지만 지금은 좋아해요.
생소하다.x: Korean food was unfamiliar at first, but now I love it.
생소하다.e: Literally 'raw and distant' — not yet familiar to you.
생소하다.t: 생소하다 is about things or ideas; for people and places 낯설다 is more common.

악의.ex: 악의는 없었지만 그의 말에 상처를 받았어요.
악의.x: He meant no harm, but I was hurt by his words.

방사선.x: Hospitals sometimes treat cancer with radiation.
방사선.t: 방사선 is the rays themselves; 방사능 is radioactivity, the ability to emit them.

냉철하다.x: The more critical the situation, the more coolly you need to judge.
냉철하다.e: Literally 'cold and penetrating' — a clear, unemotional mind.
냉철하다.t: Positive, unlike 냉정하다, which can also mean cold-hearted.

임기응변.m: improvisation, thinking on one's feet; adapting to circumstances
임기응변.ex: 발표 중에 문제가 생겼지만 임기응변으로 잘 넘겼어요.
임기응변.x: A problem came up during the presentation, but I improvised and got through it.
임기응변.e: Literally 'facing the moment, responding to change.'
임기응변.t: Can sound slightly negative, implying a stopgap: 임기응변식 대응 'a makeshift response.'

침소봉대.m: exaggeration; making a mountain out of a molehill
침소봉대.x: The media blew a small mistake way out of proportion.
침소봉대.e: Literally 'calling a small needle a big club.'

뺑소니.m: hit-and-run; running away (after doing something wrong)
뺑소니.ex: 경찰은 어젯밤 뺑소니 사고를 낸 운전자를 찾고 있어요.
뺑소니.x: Police are looking for the driver in last night's hit-and-run.
뺑소니.e: Native Korean; the verb 뺑소니치다 means 'to run off and escape'.

주춧돌.x: Honesty is the cornerstone of building trust.
주춧돌.e: 주추 'pillar base' + 돌 'stone'; the native-flavored partner of 초석.

합리론.ex: 데카르트는 근대 합리론을 대표하는 프랑스 철학자입니다.
합리론.x: Descartes is the French philosopher who represents modern rationalism.

초월적.ex: 많은 사람들이 초월적 존재에게서 위안을 얻어요.
초월적.x: Many people find comfort in a transcendent being.

공연예술.ex: 그녀는 대학에서 공연예술을 전공하고 연출가가 되었어요.
공연예술.x: She majored in performing arts in college and became a director.

능청스럽다.m: sly, coy; acting innocent with a straight face
능청스럽다.ex: 그는 아무것도 모르는 척 능청스럽게 웃었어요.
능청스럽다.x: He smiled slyly, pretending he didn't know anything.
능청스럽다.t: Not always negative: a 능청스러운 actor plays a role smoothly and naturally.
